caption: In July 2025, an AI agent deleted a production database.
It ignored the instruction to stop, and claimed the data was unrecoverable.
Nothing stood between the model and the data.
SafeRun is that missing layer, built on TrueForge.
Watch what happens when we ask it to permanently delete every 2020 rental for store 2.
A real Postgres database. Pagila. 16,044 rentals. No mocks.
Instead of obeying, SafeRun investigates through read-only MCP tools.
It maps the foreign keys and finds something we didn't know.
Every payment partition references rentals.
The 90-row delete is secretly a 180-row operation.
It surfaces this hidden blast radius
and asks which scope we actually meant.
Then it clones the entire production database and runs the delete inside the clone,
measuring the exact damage, table by table.
It writes the rollback, executes that in the clone too,
and verifies every table checksum returns to its pre-operation state.
Not “are you sure?”, but “I already tested your undo.”
It works. Here is the proof.
Only then does it stop at TrueForge's native approval gate.
A human clicks Allow.
The operation executes against production, with the verified rollback on file.
Afterwards we restored production using the agent's own rollback SQL.
Round trip proven.
The execute tool refuses, at code level, any simulation whose rollback was not verified.
The safety boundary is unpromptable.
MCP tools, skills, sandbox, approvals, ask-user questions, persistent sessions.
Every harness feature, load-bearing.
SafeRun: agents you can hand the keys to.
